title: Usability Testing Questions: What to Ask During a Session
summary: Usability testing questions that capture what users do, not what they rationalize. Probe ladders, a question bank, and a selection framework.
body_markdown:
What are usability testing questions? +


Usability testing questions are prompts that ask a participant to complete tasks or recall specific past behavior, so a usability testing or user testing session produces a behavioral trace of what participants did.


How many questions should one usability test include? +


Only the questions that map to a decision and produce evidence you can name, typically one task scenario with two or three probes per test objective. After each task, add a confidence question and an effort question, and leave opinions of the design out.


How many participants do you need for a usability test? +


For qualitative usability testing, Nielsen Norman Group research found that \[five users uncover about 85% of usability problems\](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/why-you-only-need-to-test-with-5-users/) (Nielsen, 2000), so five participants per distinct user group is a common starting point. \[Quantitative UX research\](/insights/quantitative-ux-research) needs a much larger sample, around \[40 participants per NN/g\](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/summary-quant-sample-sizes/), because usability metrics only stabilize with more data points. Participant selection matters as much as sample size, so screen participants carefully: five drawn from your target users will tell you more than twenty from outside your target audience.


What makes a usability testing question leading? +


A question is leading when it names a suspected cause. "Was the button hard to find?" supplies the explanation; "You scrolled past this area, what were you looking for?" leaves the reason to the participant.


Can you still probe in unmoderated or asynchronous sessions? +


Yes. In remote unmoderated usability testing, write tasks with clear end states, prompt think-aloud narration, and pre-write conditional follow-ups. In AI-moderated sessions, the follow-up is asked in the moment even with no researcher present.


How do scales like SUS fit with behavioral questions? +


Scales quantify how the session felt and point to where something moved, but they do not explain the cause. Use the Single Ease Question (SEQ) for per-task benchmarks and the System Usability Scale (SUS) for release-over-release comparison, then pair each score with the clip that explains it.
